summary: Two iterations of validation have confirmed that the bracket K=1 hierarchical search algorithm reliably finds the optimal TP configuration in as few as 3 evaluations, outperforming flat TPE by 33× on L40S hardware and working correctly across all tested hardware types (H100, A100, L40S) and workload seeds (42–46). The algorithm is robust even at the tightest observed TP margin of 2.1% on L40S, where flat TPE fails to converge 4 out of 5 times within a 100-evaluation budget.
key_points: Bracket K=1 achieves perfect TP selection (5/5 seeds on L40S, 25/25 seed combinations on H100) in exactly 3 evaluations by using a max-capacity profile in Phase 1, making it hardware-agnostic and immune to tight performance margins.

Flat TPE on L40S (2.1% TP margin) fails to find the global best in 4/5 seeds within 100 evaluations (median evals_to_best=101), compared to bracket K=1's deterministic 3-eval solution — a >33× speedup, substantially stronger than the predicted ≥5×; this reveals a non-linear relationship between TP margin size and TPE convergence reliability.

Still unknown: (1) whether bracket K=1 correctly selects TP=8 for qwen3-14b on L40S (different winner than llama — the only untested winner-class); (2) behavior at the combined L40S + multi-seed cross-product; (3) the rate threshold at which TP dominance transitions from TP=8 to TP=4 on each hardware type. The next iteration should test qwen3-14b on L40S to validate Phase 1 correctness when the optimal answer is TP=8 rather than TP=4.
